newsitem.title: UK: Troubled MGAM unit trust value has tumbled - paper.
newsitem.headline: Troubled MGAM unit trust value has tumbled - paper.

text.p: A Morgan Grenfell fund currently under investigation by UK investments watchdog IMRO has fallen in value 40 percent since problems in the unit trust and two other Morgan Grenfell Asset Management funds surfaced four weeks ago, the Guardian newspaper said in its Wednesday edition.

The paper said that, according to a portfolio statement sent to investors on Tuesday, the Europa Fund, which was worth 137 million stg when trading in the three funds was suspended on September 2, is now worth only 84 million stg.
It also said more than 10 percent of the fund is invested in stocks that are not listed on approved stock exchanges.
The paper said Morgan Grenfell said the true value of the Europa Fund was closer to 98 million stg, as the 84 million stg figure did not include cash holdings.

A spokesman told the paper the decline in value was partly due to redemptions, but also reflected market movements. He added that Europa's 11.76 percent holding in unlisted stocks was allowed under IMRO rules, which say investments in such stocks can exceed the 10 percent limit if the companies intend a stock market listing within 12 months, the paper said.

Deutsche Bank AG, the ultimate parent company, stepped in with a 180 million stg cash bail-out for the three funds after the discovery of irregularities and the suspension of Peter Young, the manager of two of them.

Trading in the funds was resumed after three days and Deutsche said it would support the funds for at least three months following an outflow of investor funds in the immediate aftermath of the revelation that something was wrong.

Young has since been dismissed by Morgan Grenfell and had his assets frozen. The UK's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Saturday that it had begun an investigation into Young's conduct while at Morgan Grenfell.
